source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Follows Gerasenes in the pinned text, without geographic harmonization.
key_decisions.before: They came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
key_decisions.after: They reached the other side of the sea, in the region of the Gerasenes.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.

key_decisions.rationale: Makes the confrontational idiom natural but preserves the adjuration by God and full title.
key_decisions.before: Crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”
key_decisions.after: He shouted at the top of his voice, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put you under oath by God: do not torment me!”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and crying out with a loud voice he said, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the singular-to-plural shift and leaves the unsettling reply intact.
key_decisions.before: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he asked him, “What is your name?” And he said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves singular pleading about plural spirits instead of smoothing away the shift.
key_decisions.before: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of the region.
key_decisions.after: He begged Jesus insistently not to send them out of the region.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the region.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s description without a modern medical label and keeps the observers’ surprising fear.
key_decisions.before: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been demonized sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
key_decisions.after: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had the legion. And they were afraid.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And they came to Jesus and saw the one who had been demonized sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the affectionate diminutive, urgency, requested touch, and both healing and life.
key_decisions.before: and pleaded with him earnestly, “My little daughter is near death. Come and lay your hands on her so that she may be saved and live.”
key_decisions.after: and begged him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be healed and live.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and begged him earnestly, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the explanatory inner speech and even the clothes rather than a required bodily touch.
key_decisions.before: because she kept saying, “If I touch even his clothes, I will be saved.”
key_decisions.after: For she had been saying, “If I can touch even his clothes, I will be healed.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For she was saying, “If I touch even his garments, I will be saved.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the kinship address and the healing sense of saved here; notes the broader verb separately.
key_decisions.before: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace and be healed from your affliction.”
key_decisions.after: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be free of your affliction.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed of your affliction.”

key_decisions.rationale: Uses overheard for parakousas while retaining the consequential alternative in a note.
key_decisions.before: But Jesus, overhearing what they said, told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only trust.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus overheard what they were saying and told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid. Only believe.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But Jesus, overhearing what was spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, “Do not fear; only believe.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Jesus’ startling contrast without explaining it away in the main text.
key_decisions.before: He went in and said to them, “Why are you making such a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
key_decisions.after: He went inside and said to them, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead but sleeping.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And entering, he said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
